public_rationale: Lake and Baroni's 2018 study found systematic compositional generalization failures in tested recurrent networks and tentatively linked lack of systematicity to training-data needs [e1]. Reporting available on April 8, 2024 described Meta's 2023 discussions of collecting copyrighted data despite potential lawsuits and the time required for licensing [e2]. The study does not connect its technical mechanism to those decisions, and the reporting does not isolate generalization limitations as their cause [e1, e2]. The full causal chain is neither established nor refuted [e1, e2].
limitations: The technical evidence concerns particular recurrent networks and tasks, and its link to data demand is tentative [e1].
The corporate discussions are documented through reporting based on internal recordings; the underlying records were not independently verified in this packet [e2].
The evidence does not distinguish data needed for unfamiliar facts from data needed to compensate for weak generalization in the reported decisions [e1, e2].

our_interpretation: I read greediness as needing many training examples to achieve useful performance.
I read ethical choices as consequential decisions about data collection, consent, licensing and privacy.
The claim alleges a causal chain from weak generalization to data demand and then to developer decisions. Showing large datasets and controversial conduct separately is insufficient.
The assessment concerns configurations and developer conduct by the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Technical evidence links generalization limitations to increased data needs, and documented developer decisions connect those needs to consequential collection or licensing choices.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Controlled technical evidence and documented decisions show that the alleged generalization limitation did not materially drive the data demand or the developer choices.
